news.headline: William Blair initiates uniQure at Outperform with $73 target, citing clearer AMT-130 approval path
news.summary: William Blair resumed coverage with an Outperform rating and a $73 fair value estimate, arguing AMT-130 has a clearer route to becoming the first approved disease-modifying Huntington's therapy, potentially in the US and UK in 2027. Despite the bullish note, shares faded through the following session as investors focused on the still-pending four-year data and BLA acceptance risk rather than the initiation itself.

news.headline: uniQure submits BLA to FDA and MAA to UK MHRA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease
news.summary: uniQure formally submitted a Biologics License Application to the FDA under the accelerated-approval pathway for ifezuntirgene inilparvovec (AMT-130) in Huntington's disease, alongside a parallel Marketing Authorisation Application to the UK's MHRA. The company requested priority review, which if granted would compress the FDA review to roughly six months following the standard 60-day filing review, on the strength of its RMAT, Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track designations.

news.headline: ICER opens a cost-effectiveness review of uniQure's AMT-130 with a March 2027 public meeting
news.summary: The Institute for Clinical and Economic Review launched an assessment of AMT-130 for Huntington's disease, with a scoping comment period running August 20 to September 11, 2026. A draft evidence report is due January 19, 2027, a Midwest CEPAC public meeting is set for March 25, 2027 and the final report for April 29, 2027 - the first formal US payer-value review of the therapy and an early marker for the pricing debate.

news.headline: RTW Investments and Susquehanna disclose new stakes in uniQure in 13G filings
news.summary: RTW Investments reported a beneficial stake of roughly 3.94M shares (about 5.7%) and Susquehanna-affiliated entities disclosed a 3.34M-share (4.8%) position in filings accepted by the SEC on August 14. The disclosures point to continued institutional accumulation ahead of the September AMT-130 four-year data and the Q3 BLA submission.

news.headline: Stifel reiterates Buy on uniQure with a $71 price target into the September readout
news.summary: Stifel maintained its Buy rating and $71 target, pointing to the cleared FDA accelerated-approval pathway for AMT-130 and the four-year Phase I/II data as the next major stock catalyst. Sell-side consensus now sits near a $70 average target with no sell ratings across roughly 12-22 covering analysts.

news.headline: uniQure posts Q2 2026 results: wider net loss, $810M cash runway into 2030, BLA reaffirmed for Q3
news.summary: Revenue rose 9% year over year to $5.8M while the net loss widened to $81.1M ($1.22/share) from $37.7M a year earlier; cash and investment securities stood at $810.3M, which management said funds operations into 2030. uniQure reaffirmed that four-year AMT-130 data are coming in September and that the US BLA and UK MAA submissions remain on track for Q3 2026 under the FDA-agreed accelerated-approval pathway.

catalysts.label: Four-year AMT-130 data readout
catalysts.detail: uniQure plans to report four-year topline safety and efficacy data on all 24 patients from the first two Phase I/II cohorts (12 high-dose, 12 low-dose), plus three-year follow-up on three additional high-dose patients, from a June 30, 2026 data cut. The comparison uses an updated Enroll-HD natural-history database of roughly 26,000 participants. As of September 3 the readout had not yet been announced; it remains the single biggest near-term catalyst for the stock, now landing just after rather than before the BLA/MAA filings, so it will effectively serve as a real-world check on the data package regulators are already reviewing.

catalysts.label: FDA decision on BLA acceptance and priority review
catalysts.detail: Following the September 2 BLA submission, the FDA has a standard 60-day filing review to decide whether to accept the application and whether to grant the requested priority review (which would compress the subsequent review to about six months). Acceptance and priority-review status are expected to be confirmed around November 2026, most likely disclosed alongside Q3 earnings; a PDUFA date would follow from that decision.

catalysts.label: UK MHRA review of AMT-130 MAA
catalysts.detail: The MHRA marketing authorization application, submitted in parallel with the US BLA on September 2, gives a second potential approval route independent of the FDA and a possible first-mover position in a market where no disease-modifying Huntington's therapy exists. No MHRA review timeline has been confirmed yet.

catalysts.label: ICER scoping comment deadline
catalysts.detail: ICER's public comment period on the draft scoping document for its AMT-130 cost-effectiveness review closes September 11, 2026, with a revised scoping document to follow. The framing set here shapes the value benchmark US payers will use against uniQure's eventual price.

catalysts.label: FDA advisory committee (AdCom) meeting
catalysts.detail: Management believes an advisory committee review is likely for what would be the first gene therapy for Huntington's disease and says it is preparing for one. The FDA has not confirmed a meeting or a date, and timing would follow BLA acceptance rather than submission.

catalysts.label: Confirmatory trial design finalized and initiated
catalysts.detail: The FDA requires a randomized, concurrent standard-of-care-controlled confirmatory study with Total Functional Capacity at 36 months as the primary endpoint. uniQure says it intends to start this global trial as soon as possible after the BLA submission, which has now occurred.

catalysts.label: Additional international regulatory pathways
catalysts.detail: uniQure has said it is actively pursuing further registration routes for AMT-130 beyond the US and UK, including EU options, and expects to give an update in the second half of 2026. Any added jurisdiction expands the addressable launch footprint beyond the roughly 30,000 US patients.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 results
catalysts.detail: uniQure's Q3 2026 print is expected around November 9-10, 2026, per consensus earnings-calendar estimates (not yet formally confirmed by the company). It is the first scheduled opportunity for management to confirm BLA acceptance status, whether priority review was granted, and what PDUFA date applies, and to update commercial build-out spending against the roughly $810M cash position.

catalysts.label: AMT-260 higher-dose epilepsy data and AMT-191 Fabry update
catalysts.detail: uniQure plans updated Phase I/IIa data in refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy in H1 2027, including the second, higher-dose cohort (3x10^12 gc/mL) that completed enrollment around mid-2026. First-cohort data showed 79-100% disabling-seizure reductions in three of six patients and mixed results in the other three; a Fabry (AMT-191) update is guided to the same window.

catalysts.label: Potential accelerated approval decision and ICER verdict
catalysts.detail: If the BLA is accepted with priority review, an FDA decision on the first potential Huntington's gene therapy could land around mid-2027. ICER's draft evidence report is due January 19, 2027, with a Midwest CEPAC public meeting March 25 and the final report April 29, 2027, framing the US pricing debate for a therapy expected to be priced in line with other one-time gene therapies.

pulse: QURE has pulled back to the mid-$40s (around $45-46, off a $51 intraday high on September 2) for a market cap near $3.2B after uniQure formally submitted its US BLA and UK MAA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease on September 2 and requested priority review; William Blair initiated at Outperform ($73 target) the same day, but shares faded as investors weighed that the confirmatory four-year Phase I/II data still has not been released. That readout is now the single biggest overhang since it will effectively test the data package regulators are already reviewing, alongside a still-unconfirmed FDA advisory-committee meeting and the newly opened ICER cost-effectiveness review (comment period closes September 11). Sell-side sentiment stays broadly bullish (consensus price target near $70-73, no sell ratings, continued institutional accumulation from RTW and Susquehanna in August) and the balance sheet is solid at $810.3M in cash funding operations into 2030, but the stock's next major move likely hinges on the September data drop and, later, FDA confirmation of BLA acceptance and priority-review status expected around Q3 earnings in November.
